{"candidate_rtl":"module decoder_8bit
 #(
    parameter N = 8
) (
    input [N-1:0] in,
    output reg [(1<<N)-1:0] out
);
    wire [15:0] high_decode;
    wire [15:0] low_decode;
    wire [(1<<N)-1:0] decoded;

    assign high_decode = 16'b1 << in[7:4];
    assign low_decode  = 16'b1 << in[3:0];

    genvar i;
    generate
        for (i = 0; i < (1<<N); i = i + 1) begin : gen_decode
            assign decoded[i] = high_decode[i/16] & low_decode[i%16];
        end
    endgenerate

    always @(*) begin
        out = decoded;
    end
endmodule","bottleneck":"The original 256-bit variable shift creates a wide multi-stage barrel-shifter network, making the longest path pass through several levels of muxing and producing high fanout across the output word.","rewrite":"Split the 8-bit input into two 4-bit fields, decode each field once into a 16-bit one-hot vector, and form each output bit from one high-field and one low-field decode term. This preserves the exact one-hot mapping while reducing the logic depth to two small decoders followed by one final AND level.","expected_timing_gain":"Expected lower maximum data arrival due to replacing the 8-bit, 256-wide variable shifter with shared 4-to-16 predecoders and a single output-combination level. The critical path should be approximately the depth of a 4-bit decoder plus one AND stage.","area_or_other_cost":"Uses two shared 16-bit decode networks and 256 two-input output-combination gates. This should reduce area relative to the original wide barrel shifter while remaining below the stated area cap; no sequential elements, latency, or additional I/O logic are introduced.","functional_boundaries":"For N=8, every binary input value from 0 through 255 produces exactly one asserted output bit at index equal to in, with all other bits cleared. The module name, parameter declaration/default, port widths, output reg type, combinational behavior, and 256-bit output encoding are preserved."}
